n2-set-1-q-1.translation: When she was a child, she was strictly taught manners and etiquette at home.

choices.reason: This uses the on-yomi kou for 行 instead of gyou. The sound matches other words such as 講義 (lecture) and 抗議 (protest), not the reading of 行儀.
This uses kou for 行 and leaves 儀 unvoiced as ki. The sound matches other words such as 後期 (latter period) and 好機 (good opportunity).
行儀 is read gyougi and means manners or proper behavior. 行儀がいい means well-mannered; 行儀が悪い means ill-mannered; 行儀作法 means etiquette.
The first kanji has the right reading gyou, but the second needs the voiced sound gi, not ki.

n2-set-1-q-2.translation: Winning the international competition changed the young musician's life in an instant.
n2-set-1-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: isshun - an instant or a moment

choices.reason: 一 can be read ichi elsewhere, but 一瞬 is pronounced isshun, with a doubled s sound.
This changes the first syllables and does not give the established reading of 一瞬.
This voices the second kanji as jun; 瞬 is read shun in 一瞬.
This is the standard reading of 一瞬. 一瞬にして means in an instant or suddenly.

n2-set-1-q-3.translation: Drawn in by the words 'only a few left,' I ended up buying something on a TV shopping program without thinking.

choices.reason: 誘われて is the passive form of 誘う (to invite or entice). The sales pitch tempted the speaker to buy.
This is the reading of 襲われて (being attacked), not 誘われて.
This can mean being captured or preoccupied, but it is not the reading of 誘われて.
This is associated with 歌われて (being sung), not the printed word 誘われて.

n2-set-1-q-4.translation: It used to be a quiet town, but lately there have been many unsettling incidents.

choices.reason: The second syllable is voiced as zou, but 騒 is read sou in 物騒.
物騒 is read bussou. 物騒な事件 refers to disturbing or dangerous incidents.
This omits the doubled s sound in the established reading bussou.
This both omits the doubled s sound and voices sou as zou.

n2-set-1-q-5.translation: One reason cited for the low death rate from influenza is the public's high level of hygiene knowledge.

choices.reason: 衛 is read ei, not ee, in 衛生.
The second kanji 生 is read sei here, not zei.
衛生 is read eisei and means hygiene or sanitation. 衛生知識 means knowledge of hygiene.
This changes both ei to ee and sei to zei, so it is not the reading of 衛生.

n2-set-1-q-6.translation: Products that are merely cheap have increasingly lost their appeal to consumers tired of frugal living.

choices.reason: 飯 means cooked rice or a meal; it does not write the verb akiru (to tire of).
飽きる means to grow tired of something. 飽きられて is its passive form: the products are becoming tiresome to consumers.
館 means a building or hall; it does not write the verb akiru.
飲 means to drink; it does not write the verb akiru.

n2-set-1-q-7.translation: The Tale of Genji is a representative work of classical Japanese literature.
n2-set-1-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: koten / 古典 - classical literature or a classic

choices.reason: 展 means exhibition. 古展 is not the standard spelling of koten meaning a classic.
箇 is a counter used in expressions such as 箇所. 箇典 is not the word for classical literature.
個展 is pronounced koten but means a solo exhibition, not classical literature. This is a same-sound kanji trap.
古典 means a classic or classical literature. 古典文学 is classical literature.

n2-set-1-q-8.translation: Instead of only lamenting your shortcomings, you should develop your strengths.
n2-set-1-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: nageite / 嘆いて - lamenting or grieving over

choices.reason: 難 means difficulty; 難いて is not the spelling of nageite (lamenting).
嘆いて is the te-form of 嘆く (to lament). The sentence contrasts dwelling on faults with developing strengths.
喝 relates to shouting or scolding. 喝いて is not the spelling of nageite.
漢 refers to China or a man in some compounds. 漢いて is not the spelling of nageite.

n2-set-1-q-9.translation: In today's stressful world, the number of people suffering from depression is increasing sharply.
n2-set-1-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: gekizou / 激増 - a sharp increase

choices.reason: 激 means intense or sudden, and 増 means increase. 激増する means to increase rapidly.
象 means image, phenomenon, or elephant; 激象 is not the compound for a sharp increase.
劇 means drama or a play. The established compound for a sharp increase uses 激, not 劇.
Neither 劇 nor 象 forms the established word 激増 here.

n2-set-1-q-10.translation: Thanks to advanced technology, seawater has been turned into fresh water and made drinkable.

choices.reason: 単 means single or simple. 単水 is not the word for fresh water.
短 means short. 短水 is not the word for fresh water.
淡水 means fresh water. 淡水化 is the process of making seawater fresh or drinkable.
探 means to search. 探水 is not the word for fresh water.

n2-set-1-q-11.translation: Writing characters by hand is said to improve your memory.

choices.reason: 質 means quality, but 記憶質 is not the natural compound for one's ability to remember.
化 means change or transformation. 記憶化 does not fit the idea of memory ability here.
力 means ability or power. 記憶力 is the standard word for memory capacity, which can 高まる (improve).
性 means nature or tendency. 記憶性 is not the standard word for memory ability in this sentence.

n2-set-1-q-12.translation: This painting is a representative work of his.
n2-set-1-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: daihyou-saku / 代表作 - a representative work

choices.reason: 品 means an item or product. For a painting as an artist's signature work, the standard compound is 代表作.
作 means a created work. 代表作 is an artist's notable or representative work.
物 means a thing. 代表物 is not the standard expression for an artist's representative work.
者 means a person. 代表者 means a representative person, not a painting.

n2-set-1-q-13.translation: This is a protected area for alpine plants.
n2-set-1-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: hogo-ku / 保護区 - protected area or reserve

choices.reason: 区 means district or zone. 保護区 is an area designated for protection, fitting alpine plants.
場 means a place or site, but 保護場 is not the standard term for a protected area.
所 means a place or facility. 保護所 would suggest a facility, not a protected natural zone.
域 means region, but 保護域 is not the standard term used here; 保護区 is.

n2-set-1-q-14.translation: The official professional baseball season is about to begin.
n2-set-1-q-14.correctAnswerEnglish: 公式戦 (koushiki-sen) - an official match or game

choices.reason: 軍 means an army; 公式軍 is not the term for an official baseball game.
陣 means a camp or formation; 公式陣 does not name a match.
戦 means a contest or match. 公式戦 is a formally scheduled game, as opposed to an exhibition game.
権 means a right or authority; 公式権 does not describe a baseball game.

n2-set-1-q-15.translation: This medicine has the side effect of irritating the stomach.

choices.reason: 悪 means bad or evil, but 悪作用 is not the standard medical term for a side effect.
副 means secondary. 副作用 is an unintended effect in addition to a medicine's main effect.
複 means multiple or complex; 複作用 is not the standard word for a medicine's side effect.
反 means opposite or anti-. 反作用 means a reaction or counteraction, not the standard term for this medical side effect.

n2-set-1-q-16.translation: People say history repeats itself, but things almost never repeat in exactly the same way.
n2-set-1-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: 滅多にない (metta ni nai) - almost never happens

choices.reason: 眼中 means in one's consideration. 眼中にない means to disregard something, not that it rarely happens.
滅多にない is the fixed expression for something that hardly ever occurs.
まれ means rare, but まれにない is not the natural construction; まれにある would mean it occasionally happens.
たま means occasionally in expressions such as たまに, but たまにない does not fit this sentence.

n2-set-1-q-17.translation: If the washing machine breaks down this often, there is no choice but to replace it.

choices.reason: それぞれ means each or respectively; it does not describe repeated breakdowns.
しばしば means frequently. Repeated failures motivate replacing the machine.
ぞくぞく means one after another, often for people or things arriving, and is not natural for one machine repeatedly breaking down.
とうとう means finally or at last; it describes an eventual outcome rather than frequent failures.

n2-set-1-q-18.translation: Many elderly people live alone in this area, and there are concerns about security.
n2-set-1-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: セキュリティー (sekyuriti) - security or safety protection

choices.reason: セキュリティー refers to security or protective measures. セキュリティーに不安がある means there are security concerns.
コンディション means condition or physical state, not protection from threats in this context.
オペレーション means operation or management of a process; it does not naturally express these residents' security concerns.
コンタクト means contact, such as communication or a contact lens, not security.

n2-set-1-q-19.translation: My dream is to be active on a global stage.
n2-set-1-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: 舞台 (butai) - a stage or arena for activity

choices.reason: 信頼 means trust; グローバルな信頼で活躍 is not the expression for working internationally.
資本 means capital or assets; it does not provide the figurative arena intended here.
舞台 literally means stage and figuratively means an arena. グローバルな舞台で活躍する means to succeed internationally.
現実 means reality; グローバルな現実で活躍 is not the intended collocation.

n2-set-1-q-20.translation: The way this house is built is unique to this region.
n2-set-1-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: 独特 (dokutoku) - distinctive or unique to

choices.reason: 独特 means distinctive. この地方独特のもの means something characteristic of this area.
格別 means exceptional or especially, but 地方格別のもの is not the natural phrase for a local building style.
特例 means an exception to a rule, not a distinctive regional style.
特殊 means special or unusual, but この地方特殊のもの is not the standard collocation; 独特 specifically means unique to this place.

n2-set-1-q-21.translation: While repairing the roof, we decided to install a solar power generation system.
n2-set-1-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: 修繕 (shuuzen) - repair or maintenance of a building

choices.reason: 調節 means adjustment, such as changing a level or setting; it does not mean repairing a roof.
管理 means management or upkeep in a broad sense, not the specific repair implied by the work on the roof.
修正 means correction of an error or revision of text or plans, not repairing physical damage to a roof.
修繕 means to repair a damaged building or object. 屋根を修繕する is a natural collocation.

n2-set-1-q-22.translation: I use clippings from newspaper cooking articles as a reference when planning meals.
n2-set-1-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: 切り抜き (kirinuki) - a clipping cut from a newspaper or magazine

choices.reason: 切り抜き is a clipping removed from a newspaper or magazine, which can be saved for reference.
切り取り means cutting or tearing off a portion, but it does not specifically name a saved newspaper clipping here.
書き取り means dictation or writing down what one hears, not an article cut out of a paper.
選り抜き means a selection of the best items, not a physical newspaper clipping.

n2-set-1-q-23.translation: This private railway connects with JR at the next station.
n2-set-1-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: つながっている (tsunagatte iru) - is connected

choices.reason: 乗り換えになる refers to a transfer; it is related to rail travel but does not directly mean that the lines connect.
交差している means crossing or intersecting; mere crossing does not imply a connecting service.
一体化している means being integrated into one; the private line and JR remain separate systems.
連絡している means the lines link or connect at the station. つながっている is the matching paraphrase.

n2-set-1-q-24.translation: The election prediction turned out to be wrong.
n2-set-1-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: 当たらなかった (ataranakatta) - did not turn out to be correct

choices.reason: 騒がれた means caused a stir or was talked about; it says nothing about whether the prediction was right.
おかしかった means was strange or funny, not that the forecast failed.
予想が外れた means the prediction missed. 当たらなかった expresses the same result in the negative.
難しかった means was difficult; a difficult prediction might still be correct.

n2-set-1-q-25.translation: Even though I took a shortcut, it ended up taking more time instead.
n2-set-1-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: 逆に (gyaku ni) - conversely or instead

choices.reason: 非常に means very or extremely; it gives degree, not an unexpected reversal.
改めて means anew or once again; it does not express a contrary outcome.
かえって means contrary to expectation. 逆に captures the reversal: a shortcut took longer.
多少 means somewhat or to some extent, not the opposite of the expected result.

n2-set-1-q-26.translation: To state my opinion plainly, I am opposed to that proposal.
n2-set-1-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: 率直に (socchoku ni) - frankly or candidly

choices.reason: はっきり means clearly or plainly here. 率直に means speaking frankly without hiding one's view.
適当に means suitably or casually, sometimes carelessly; it does not mean expressing one's position clearly.
簡単に means simply or briefly, but a brief opinion need not be candid or unambiguous.
自由に means freely; it concerns permission, not clarity or frankness of speech.

n2-set-1-q-27.translation: The supervisor came to work on a day off and covered for the subordinate's delayed work.
n2-set-1-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: 補った (oginatta) - made up for or compensated for a shortfall

choices.reason: 進めた means advanced the work; it does not specifically mean making up for someone else's shortfall.
終わらせた means finished it; the sentence does not establish that all the work was completed.
引き受けた means accepted responsibility for a task, but カバーした emphasizes filling the gap left by the subordinate.
カバーした means covered or compensated for the delayed work. 補った is the closest paraphrase.

n2-set-1-q-28.translation: Choose the sentence that correctly uses tsuuyou, meaning to work or be accepted in a situation.
n2-set-1-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: 通用する (tsuuyou suru) - to be valid, work, or be accepted

choices.reason: This says they plan to 'tsuuyou' a capable person for the job. 通用 cannot mean hire or employ; 採用する would fit.
This says, 'Such a poor excuse won't work on me.' 言い訳が通用しない is a natural use of 通用する.
This says the pay will not 'tsuuyou' for a dangerous job. The intended idea is insufficient pay, not whether an excuse or ability works.
This says the book will 'tsuuyou' for your studies. 役に立つ, meaning be useful, would be natural instead.

n2-set-1-q-29.translation: Choose the sentence that correctly uses arasuji, meaning the outline or plot of a story.
n2-set-1-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: あらすじ (arasuji) - an outline or story synopsis

choices.reason: This says, 'My paper is arasuji finished.' あらすじ is a noun for an outline, not an adverb meaning almost.
This says the 'arasuji' of a management policy was decided at a meeting. 方針 or 概要 would be more natural for a policy.
This says friends got into a fierce 'arasuji.' A quarrel or argument would be 争い or 口論, not a synopsis.
This says, 'Summarize the plot of this novel in no more than 400 characters.' あらすじ naturally names a novel's synopsis.

n2-set-1-q-30.translation: Choose the sentence that correctly uses meiwaku, meaning trouble or inconvenience caused to others.
n2-set-1-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: 迷惑 (meiwaku) - nuisance or inconvenience to someone else

choices.reason: This says everyone has one or two 'meiwaku memories.' A troublesome or unpleasant memory is not normally described as 迷惑な思い出.
This says, 'Opening a newspaper on a crowded train inconveniences other passengers.' 他の客に迷惑だ is a natural use.
This says the family's life is a 'good nuisance' on a low salary. 迷惑 does not describe the family's standard of living.
This says the illness was already in a 'nuisance state.' 手遅れ or 深刻 would describe a late or serious condition, not 迷惑.

n2-set-1-q-31.translation: Choose the sentence that correctly uses baibai, meaning the buying and selling of goods or property.
n2-set-1-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: 売買 (baibai) - buying and selling; a commercial transaction

choices.reason: This says the store 'baibai-s' even on weekends. A store can 営業する, be open for business, but bare 売買する does not describe its opening days naturally.
This says the product's 'baibai' is good and production cannot keep up. 売れ行き, sales performance, is the natural expression.
This says the speaker decided to 'buy and sell' this plot of land because of circumstances. If only selling is meant, 売る is clearer; the printed answer uses an actual property transaction.
This says, 'A qualification is required to buy and sell real estate.' 不動産を売買する naturally describes property transactions.

n2-set-1-q-32.translation: Choose the sentence that correctly uses kahansuu, meaning more than half of a defined group.
n2-set-1-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: 過半数 (kahansuu) - a majority, more than half

choices.reason: This says a new bill passed after gaining a majority of votes in favor. 過半数の賛成 is the standard expression.
This says the number of earthquake victims was 'a majority' without specifying the group of which they were more than half.
This says fans rushed to the small venue 'in a majority.' 過半数 is a proportion of a defined total, not an adverb for crowd size.
This says evidence that he is guilty is 'a majority.' Evidence is not naturally counted as a majority in this construction.

n2-set-1-q-33.translation: I decided to change jobs after thinking it through carefully, so I do not mind even if it fails.
n2-set-1-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: よく考えた上で (yoku kangaeta ue de) - after careful consideration

choices.reason: 際に means at the time of doing something; it does not express deciding after considering the result.
あげく means after a long process that ends unfavorably. The decision itself is not presented as that kind of bad outcome.
Verb past form plus 上で means after doing something and taking it into account. The decision follows careful thought.
ついでに means while doing something else or taking the opportunity to do another thing; the decision is not incidental.

n2-set-1-q-34.translation: A tax increase would be difficult. But given the reality that the elderly population keeps growing, it cannot be helped.
n2-set-1-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: 現実からいって (genjitsu kara itte) - judging from that reality

choices.reason: からいって uses a fact as the basis for a judgment: given the growing elderly population, the increase seems unavoidable.
だからといって means even so or that does not mean. It introduces a counterpoint, not the factual basis for 仕方がない here.
だけあって means as one would expect given a notable quality. It does not mark this social reality as the reason for a judgment.
といって means saying or even if one says; it does not express 'judging from the reality' in this sentence.

n2-set-1-q-35.translation: The Thai food here has been made a little less spicy for Japanese customers.
n2-set-1-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: 日本人向けに (nihonjin-muke ni) - tailored for Japanese people

choices.reason: 的に forms an adverb such as 'typically' with some nouns; 日本人的に does not express a target audience for the recipe.
用に suggests something for a concrete use, such as equipment or a designated room. Here the food is adapted to an audience.
寄りに means closer to or leaning toward, not prepared for the tastes of a particular group.
向けに means aimed or tailored for a group. The restaurant has adjusted the spice level for Japanese diners.

n2-set-1-q-36.translation: As far as I have seen, I do not think Yamada is such a bad person.
n2-set-1-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: 見たかぎりでは (mita kagiri de wa) - as far as I have seen

choices.reason: ことでは does not form the expression 'as far as I have seen' after 見た.
ものでは does not mark the limits of one's observation in this sentence.
Past verb plus かぎりでは limits the judgment to what the speaker has observed.
まででは is not the grammatical pattern used to state the bounds of what one has seen.

n2-set-1-q-37.translation: If you say you could do it better yourself, then you should try doing it.
n2-set-1-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: やってみることだ (yatte miru koto da) - you should try doing it

choices.reason: わけだ explains a logical conclusion or reason; it does not express the pointed advice intended here.
ものだ can state a general norm, but this speaker is directly challenging the listener to try it.
Verb dictionary form plus ことだ gives advice. In this sentence the advice carries a mildly sarcastic challenge.
はずだ means something is expected or should be the case; it does not tell the listener to take action.

n2-set-1-q-38.translation: While more women continue working after marriage, more women also want to become full-time homemakers.
n2-set-1-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: 一方で (ippou de) - on the other hand; meanwhile

choices.reason: 反対で means being opposed or opposite, but 増える反対で is not the grammatical contrast pattern here.
以外で means outside of or apart from, not a contrast between two concurrent trends.
片面で is not the standard connective for presenting two sides of a situation.
一方で connects two contrasting facts: growth in women continuing work and growth in women preferring homemaking.

n2-set-1-q-39.translation: I was so worried about the test results that I could not sleep until morning.
n2-set-1-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: 心配のあまり (shinpai no amari) - from excessive worry

choices.reason: Noun plus のあまり expresses an excessive feeling that produces a result. Strong worry kept the speaker awake.
のせいか means perhaps because of; it expresses uncertainty rather than the strong degree of worry emphasized here.
のくせに means despite or even though, usually with criticism, and conflicts with the cause-and-result meaning.
のおかげで credits a beneficial cause. Being unable to sleep is not a benefit.

n2-set-1-q-40.translation: Because this fruit is very good for your health, it has long been called 'doctor-not-needed.'
n2-set-1-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: ことから (koto kara) - because of the fact that

choices.reason: ことから connects a known fact to the reason for a name or conclusion: its health benefits explain the nickname.
ことだから means given someone's known character or nature; it does not supply this factual reason for the fruit's name.
ことに can introduce an evaluative remark, such as 驚いたことに, but not this cause for the nickname.
ことなら means if it is about or if one is going to do something; it does not explain why the fruit is named this way.

n2-set-1-q-41.translation: Although I know smoking is bad for my health, I just cannot quit.
n2-set-1-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: 知りつつも (shiri tsutsu mo) - although I know

choices.reason: Verb stem plus つつも expresses a contrast: knowing the harm but continuing to smoke.
知らないものの means despite not knowing; it reverses the fact that the speaker knows smoking is harmful.
知るからには means now that one knows, implying a responsibility, not this contrast with inability to quit.
知らないくせに means despite not knowing, often with reproach; it contradicts the speaker's knowledge.

n2-set-1-q-42.translation: If no one else here has a license, I have no choice but to drive, do I?
n2-set-1-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: 運転しないわけにはいかない (unten shinai wake ni wa ikanai) - cannot avoid driving

choices.reason: するわけにはいかない means cannot do it; it would say the speaker is unable or not allowed to drive.
The double negative means one cannot avoid doing something. The speaker feels obliged to drive.
するべきでない means should not drive, the opposite of the intended necessity.
してはいられない means cannot keep doing it; it does not express having to start driving.

n2-set-1-q-43.translation: Even if you did not like the gift, you should at least write a thank-you letter to the person who gave it to you.
n2-set-1-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: 気に入らなかったにしても (ki ni iranakatta ni shite mo) - even if you did not like it

choices.reason: たとえ plus にしても expresses a concession: thanks are still expected even if the gift was unwelcome.
としたら makes an ordinary hypothetical condition. With たとえ, the sentence requires the concessive 'even if' meaning.
気に入ったとしても means even if you liked it, which does not make the intended contrast with the duty to thank someone.
気に入ったとしたら means if you liked it; both the polarity and conditional meaning miss the concession.

n2-set-1-q-44.translation: A: 'Unfortunately, Tanaka is out.' B: 'Then could you please tell Tanaka that Yamada from Company A called?'
n2-set-1-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: お伝えいただけますか (otsutae itadakemasu ka) - could you please pass on the message?

choices.reason: 伝えていただきますか is not the natural polite request form; いただけますか asks whether the other person could do the favor.
お plus verb stem plus いただけますか politely asks the listener to convey the message.
お伝えになれますか uses honorific language awkwardly here; it does not express the standard request for this favor.
お伝えいたしましょうか means 'Shall I tell them?', offering the speaker's own action instead of asking the listener.

n2-set-1-q-45.translation: If you think you can pass with that way of studying, go ahead and try it.
n2-set-1-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: やれるものなら (yareru mono nara) - if you can really do it

choices.reason: やれる means 'can do it' and follows できるか in the sentence order; it does not occupy the marked third blank.
やって means 'try/do it' and connects to みればいいよ at the end, so it belongs in the fourth blank.
できるか means 'whether you can pass' and starts the sequence after 合格.
ものなら follows the potential form やれる to form a challenging conditional. The complete order is できるか, やれる, ものなら, やって.

n2-set-1-q-46.translation: Japanese people tend to forget how fortunate they are to have free drinking water everywhere.
n2-set-1-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: 忘れがち (wasuregachi) - tend to forget

choices.reason: がち is a suffix meaning 'tend to'; it completes 忘れがち at the end, so it is the fourth blank.
飲める means 'can drink' and describes 水 at the start of the four-part phrase.
忘れ is the verb stem meaning 'forget'; it pairs with がち to express a habitual tendency. It is the marked third blank.
ありがたさを means 'the value or blessing of it' plus an object marker. It follows 飲める and precedes 忘れ.

n2-set-1-q-47.translation: Going to the dentist does not necessarily become easy just because you become an adult.
n2-set-1-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: というものではありません (to iu mono de wa arimasen) - it is not necessarily the case that

choices.reason: なれば means 'if/when one becomes' and follows 大人に in the first blank.
という joins 平気になる to ものではありません, which rejects a simplistic generalization. It occupies the marked third blank.
ものでは completes the negative pattern というものではありません at the end, so it is the fourth blank.
平気になる means 'become comfortable with it' and follows 大人になれば before という.

n2-set-1-q-48.translation: Just because I forgot to lock the house, a burglar broke in.
n2-set-1-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: かけるのを忘れたばかりに (kakeru no o wasureta bakari ni) - solely because I forgot to lock it

choices.reason: 忘れた means 'forgot' and follows かけるのを. It is the marked second blank.
に completes the causal pattern ばかりに immediately before the bad result, so it is the fourth blank.
かけるのを nominalizes 'locking' as the thing forgotten; it starts the four-part sequence.
ばかり means 'just/only' and combines with に to mark the unfortunate cause; it belongs after 忘れた.

n2-set-1-q-49.translation: A: 'I no longer have a fever, and I have an exam, so I can go to school, right?' B: 'Since there is a risk of passing the illness to others, you had better stay home from school.'
n2-set-1-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: うつすおそれがある以上は (utsusu osore ga aru ijou wa) - since there is a risk of spreading it

choices.reason: ある follows おそれが to complete 'there is a risk'; it occupies the third blank, not the marked second.
以上は means 'since that is the case' and introduces the obligation to stay home; it is the final blank.
うつす means 'transmit' and follows 病気を人に at the start of the phrase.
おそれが means 'a risk of' and follows うつす. It occupies the marked second blank in the order うつす, おそれが, ある, 以上は.

n2-set-1-q-50.translation: Not so long ago, most Japanese households used to have equipment for the game of go. Children learned the rules by watching older people play.
n2-set-1-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: あったものだ (atta mono da) - used to have, recalling the past

choices.reason: ことだ gives advice or states a point; it does not reminisce about a past custom.
Past verb plus ものだ recalls what habitually happened in the past, matching the description of old households.
ところだ marks a point in time, such as about to do or just did something; it does not describe a former custom.
ようだ means it appears or seems so; the author is describing a remembered past habit, not guessing.

n2-set-1-q-51.translation: As go's playing population fell and few children took it up, people involved in the game felt deep anxiety about its future in Japan.
n2-set-1-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: 強い不安を持っていた (tsuyoi fuan o motte ita) - had strong concerns

choices.reason: 大きな希望を持っていた means held great hope; it conflicts with the falling number of players.
The decline from roughly 12 million players to around 3 million, with few children, explains their strong anxiety.
安心しかねなかった is not the natural expression here. The context explicitly requires anxiety about the future.
少しの心配もなかった means had no worries at all, the opposite of the concern caused by the decline.

n2-set-1-q-52.translation: A hit manga about go became the starting point for roughly a million children to take up the game.
n2-set-1-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: きっかけ (kikkake) - trigger or starting point

choices.reason: このマンガをきっかけとして means 'using this manga as the occasion or catalyst.' It explains why children started playing.
もと means base or origin, but このマンガをもとして is not the natural expression for a motivating event.
事情 means circumstances; it does not name the trigger that made children begin playing go.
原因 means cause, but このマンガを原因として is unnatural here and often suggests a problematic result.

n2-set-1-q-53.translation: In fact, the number of people newly taking up go is already declining.
n2-set-1-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: 減りつつある (heri tsutsu aru) - is gradually decreasing

choices.reason: Verb stem plus つつある expresses an ongoing change. It supports the warning that the manga boom may be temporary.
減りそうもない means shows no sign of decreasing; that would contradict the author's warning about a fading boom.
増えるかもしれない means might increase; the next sentence instead discusses preventing the boom from ending.
増えざるを得ない means cannot help but increase; neither the context nor the author's concern supports an inevitable increase.

n2-set-1-q-54.translation: People involved are trying many ideas because they do not want this opportunity to end as a temporary fad.
n2-set-1-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: 終わらせまい (owarasemai) - determined not to let it end

choices.reason: 終わらせたい means want to end it, opposite to the effort to sustain interest in go.
終わらせよう means let us end it, again opposite to the ideas being proposed.
The negative volitional まい expresses a firm intention not to let the opportunity end as a passing boom.
終わりたくない means do not want to end, but the people are trying not to let the boom end; the causative 終わらせまい fits their active prevention.
